openings.claim: Unreliable storage addresses may drive delays. Maintain a movement-updated locator tied to the reserving reader; cart retention may remain efficient, so alphabetical shelving need not be replaced.
openings.discriminator: Verified identities and locations should reduce second searches; persistent peak delays with little searching favor the arrival-burst rival.
openings.probe: Compare matched pickups before and during updates; record arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, location accuracy, second searches and update work. Stop at the preparation cap.
openings.uncertainty: Fit covers the capped probe only. Identity-check capability and sustained feasibility are unconfirmed; match arrival volume and book size. All evidence is synthetic.

openings.claim: Couple divider ranges to exception-slip bands: a current matching entry routes directly to the cart or recorded location before shelf searching. Region routing still requires recipient verification.
openings.discriminator: An intact range-to-row link must outperform scrambled links with identical accurate contents and an uncoupled current slip; otherwise coupling adds no demonstrated advantage.
openings.probe: Rehearse baseline, cards alone, slip alone, coupled routing and scrambled-link routing with matched moves, household mismatches and peak workload; report incompletion at the cap.
openings.uncertainty: Marking and movement corrections may exceed the budget. Persistent second searches, wrong-reader handoffs or excess preparation defeat advantage or fit; rehearsal only provisionally predicts evening performance.

decision: Test locator repair and coupling separately under one-clerk handoffs, names/contact details behind the desk, existing two shelves/cart, and ten total daily preparation minutes including corrections. Verify recipient identity. Neither establishes 95% completion within two minutes or zero wrong-reader handoffs. Household-mismatch causality and reader-interview representativeness remain unknown.
